transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-21 16:00 PDT | duration ~52m | attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Anand (CISO - Vanguard Biotech), Marcus Lee (Head of Platform), Tara Singh (DevSecOps)

Summary: quick intro, then deep into compliance and deployment model choices; emphasis on PHI handling, KMS, and audit logging granularity.

00:00 - Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Ava, the AE, and Diego is our SE.
00:08 - Dr. Priya Anand: Hi, Priya here, CISO at Vanguard. Marcus and Tara are on as well.
00:13 - Marcus Lee: Hey all.
00:15 - Tara Singh: Hi.
00:21 - Ava Chen: Great. We put together a short agenda: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML, RBAC/audit logs, encryption/KMS options, data retention, and then next steps and pilot scoping. Sound good?
00:33 - Dr. Priya Anand: Yep. Our timeline is pretty accelerated, we need a compliant inference solution for some PHI-adjacent workloads by Q3. We want to narrow Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
00:45 - Diego Marquez: Totally understood. Quick call-out on nomenclature "Hosted" means Redwood-managed multi-tenant endpoints with our compliance stack, "Dedicated" is customer-dedicated capacity in our cloud with isolation and SLAs, and "Private" is VPC or on-prem deployment where you control network/KMS.
01:05 - Marcus Lee: Can you share what controls are in scope for your SOC 2? We need specifics - encryption, key management, pen test results.
01:15 - Ava Chen: Yes. We'll send the SOC 2 Type II report and ISO27001 certificate after this call. High-level: encryption at rest and in transit, RBAC, audit logs retention, vulnerability management and regular pen testing.
01:29 - Dr. Priya Anand: Is your SOC2 covering dedicated instances as well or only hosted?
01:34 - Diego Marquez: The SOC2 is for our control plane and hosted service operations; Dedicated includes the same control processes and additional contractual protections. For Private deployments, customers take on some responsibilities — we provide the control mappings and third-party attestations where applicable.
01:56 - Tara Singh: About encryption, can we bring our own KMS? We need customer-managed keys for certain datasets.
02:03 - Diego Marquez: Yes, for Private we support customer-managed KMS (we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and we also support a KMS integration for Dedicated with Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) flows. For Hosted multi-tenant we can offer a service-managed key but for PHI we usually recommend Dedicated with BYOK or Private for full separation.
02:28 - Marcus Lee: What about HSM-backed keys / FIPS compliance?
02:32 - Diego Marquez: We have options to support HSM-backed keys via our KMS integrations; specifics depend on the cloud provider and region. We can share details on FIPS modules and HSM attestation in the docs we send.
02:49 - Dr. Priya Anand: Audit logs — we need per-request logs including caller identity, request payload hash, model used, tokens generated, and timestamps. Retention should be configurable up to 7 years.
03:02 - Diego Marquez: Our audit logging captures request metadata and authentication identity; payloads are redacted by default in hosted to protect PII, but for Dedicated/Private you can opt to retain raw request/response logs subject to agreements. Retention windows are configurable, and we can push logs to your SIEM or S3.
03:25 - Tara Singh: How granular is RBAC? Can we map to Okta groups and restrict model access per team and per route?
03:31 - Ava Chen: Yes, Redwood supports RBAC at the token/route/model level. You can map SAML groups to roles and apply policies at route or model scope. We also support SCIM provisioning to sync groups.
03:45 - Marcus Lee: SSO specifically — is SAML 2.0 the primary option? We do OIDC as well.
03:51 - Diego Marquez: We support SAML 2.0 and OIDC. For enterprise customers we typically do SAML + SCIM. We'll put the IdP metadata template in the runbook.
04:05 - Dr. Priya Anand: Data residency — our data must remain in EU for certain projects. Do you have EU-only hosting?
04:12 - Ava Chen: Yes, we have region-based routing and can pin workloads to EU-hosted infrastructure. For Dedicated you can select region allocation; Private deployments can be within your VPC in EU or on-prem.
04:27 - Marcus Lee: Any differences in audit scope or evidence if we pick Dedicated in EU vs Hosted EU?
04:33 - Diego Marquez: The control processes are consistent; the difference is deployment and contractual commitments. We'll provide control mappings that show how SOC2/ISO controls map to Dedicated and Private deployments, and any gaps are documented.
04:48 - Tara Singh: Pen tests — do you do internal and external pen testing and can we get the reports or an ATO package?
04:55 - Ava Chen: We do regular third-party pen tests and vulnerability scans. We can provide summary reports and work with your security team on an ATO package. Detailed pen test reports are shared under an NDA.
05:07 - Dr. Priya Anand: Regarding retention/deletion APIs — can we purge model context and embeddings on demand? We need both bulk deletion and record-level deletion with proof.
05:18 - Diego Marquez: Yes, we expose deletion APIs for artifacts including logs, model cache/prefixes, and embeddings. For Hosted there is a standard retention policy and deletion workflow; for Dedicated/Private you have more control and can request immediate purges. We can also provide deletion audit evidence.
05:39 - Marcus Lee: On the technical side — network topology for Dedicated: do we run in our VPC or in your cloud tenant with VPC peering? We prefer VPC peering for easier control over egress.
05:53 - Diego Marquez: For Dedicated we offer both patterns: customer VPC peering (preferred) or private links depending on cloud. For Private on-prem we ship an appliance or containerized bundle. We'll detail supported patterns in the tech deep-dive.
06:12 - Tara Singh: Are there any known limitations around KV cache or persistent state that might store sensitive info? We need guarantee that model cache won't persist PHI beyond the request unless configured.
06:24 - Diego Marquez: Our KV cache is per-request and can be configured to avoid long-term persistence; by default we don't persist raw input past model caching for latency unless caching is explicitly enabled. For PHI workloads we'd recommend disabling prefix caching or using Dedicated with explicit retention policies. We'll include docs on cache behavior.
06:45 - Dr. Priya Anand: How do you handle customer access to logs and the console — is there session-level logging and MFA enforcement?
06:52 - Ava Chen: We enforce MFA for all Redwood Console access for customers. We log admin sessions, and we can configure session timeout and SSO enforcement. Logs can be exported to your SIEM.
07:05 - Marcus Lee: From a legal side, do you sign BAAs for PHI?
07:09 - Ava Chen: We do support BAA for enterprise customers; that is part of our Private/Dedicated contractual offering. We'll surface the legal checklist and BAA template.
07:18 - Tara Singh: For encryption-in-transit, do you support mutual TLS between our services and Redwood endpoints?
07:24 - Diego Marquez: We support mTLS for Dedicated/private peering scenarios; for hosted public endpoints we use standard TLS with client tokens. mTLS is available for customer-managed private links.
07:41 - Dr. Priya Anand: Are there any throughput/latency tradeoffs when using BYOK or mTLS?
07:46 - Diego Marquez: Minimal — key lookup and HSM operations add milliseconds per key operation, but we cache key material where allowed. We'll include expected latency deltas in the benchmark doc.
07:58 - Marcus Lee: Speaking of benchmarks, we want to run a 2-week pilot and validate cost per token and p95 latency for our typical sequences (average 800 tokens per call, peak concurrency ~40). Can Redwood support that kind of pilot?
08:14 - Ava Chen: Yes, that's exactly the kind of pilot we run. We'll propose a pilot matrix and success criteria. Diego will lead the bench plan.
08:24 - Diego Marquez: For pilot planning, I'll need sample traces, expected RPS, and a set of prompts to reproduce. We'll instrument metrics and share dashboards and request-level audit logs as part of the trial.
08:38 - Tara Singh: If we go Dedicated, how does patching and maintenance work? Do you manage kernel and runtime updates?
08:47 - Diego Marquez: For Dedicated we manage the Redwood runtime and apply security patches as part of our SLA. For Private on-prem, customers manage the host OS but we provide guidance and patches for the Redwood runtime. We'll clarify in the runbook.
09:03 - Dr. Priya Anand: One more on RBAC: can we integrate with our existing ABAC policies or do you only support role-based?
09:10 - Diego Marquez: Primary support is RBAC with group-to-role mapping but we can support attributes in policies via OIDC claims for ABAC-like behavior. We'll document how to map attributes and provide examples.
09:25 - Marcus Lee: Do you provide immutable audit trails for compliance? We want tamper-evident logs.
09:31 - Ava Chen: We can stream logs to your immutable store or S3 with object lock for immutability, and provide signed audit proofs where required.
09:44 - Tara Singh: Regarding data minimization, do you have built-in PII redaction or DLP integrations?
09:51 - Diego Marquez: We have basic PII redaction heuristics and integration points for third-party DLP solutions. For sensitive workloads we recommend Dedicated/Private with customer-side DLP.
10:05 - Dr. Priya Anand: Ok this is helpful. Can you also include threat modeling notes for how model output can leak sensitive infomation and what mitigations exist?
10:15 - Ava Chen: Yes, Diego has worked on model safety and we'll include mitigations: prompt filtering, response filters, and monitoring/regression alerts via Redwood Optimize.
10:26 - Marcus Lee: Any limitations around federated identity for dev tokens — can devs get short-lived tokens with scoped access?
10:33 - Diego Marquez: Yes we support short-lived tokens via our token issuance flow and can map them to roles. We'll include examples for CI/CD patterns.
10:45 - Tara Singh: For the pilot, we will need an expected cost estimate. Can you share cost per token ranges for q4 models and for quantized variants?
10:54 - Ava Chen: We'll share pricing ranges and a cost-estimation worksheet. For pilots we often grant credits to run initial load tests.
11:05 - Dr. Priya Anand: Great. Anything else on your side?
11:09 - Ava Chen: Just to recap next steps and owners. Diego will send technical runbooks (SSO, KMS, networking), I'll send compliance artifacts and pricing/pilot proposal, Marcus/Tara will share sample traffic and PHI scope.
11:24 - Marcus Lee: We'll compile and get back by Friday.
11:27 - Tara Singh: Thanks everyone.
11:30 - Ava Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the deep dive.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings - e.g., "ATO" recorded as "A T O" sometimes; some product names spelled variably (e.g., KMS, KeyVautl).

End of call.
